## The symptom

A `defineTool` works fine from your scoped SU session but fails **fleet-wide** for
cups / unscoped psu sessions with:

```
built-in tool "memory:list" requires a workspace-scoped call — this session has
no workspace transaction. Scope the session to a workspace, or pass a per-call
workspace where the host/tool supports one.
```

It's **deterministic** (same shape every call) and **scope-dependent**: a session
that resolved a workspace (most interactive SU sessions) never reproduces it, so
it hides until a cup or an unscoped psu session hits it. This is what the
improvement-watchdog filed as EI-177 / EI-178 / EI-210 (memory:search / remember /
list).

## Why

The MCP host resolves `ctx.workspaceId` to `'*'` for an unscoped session
(`_mcp-handler.ts`). Principal-gated tools are then run inside a workspace
transaction by default — and a `'*'` session has none, so the projected gate
refuses the call with `workspace_required`.

But some tools are **workspace-agnostic by design**: their tables are scoped by
`user-id` / `harness-slug`, never by a workspace transaction. The memory store is
the canonical example (it reads `getMemoryBackend()`, never `ctx.tx`). For these,
the gate is simply wrong to apply.

## The fix

Declare **`crossWorkspace: true`** on the `defineTool` definition.
`definePrincipalGatedTool` threads it, handing an unscoped superuser session the
admin handle + a synthesized principal instead of failing `workspace_required`:

```ts
export default defineTool({
  name: 'memory:list',
  capability: 'memory:read',
  // The store is workspace-agnostic (tables scoped by user-id / harness-slug,
  // not by a workspace tx; handler reads getMemoryBackend, never ctx.tx).
  crossWorkspace: true,
  args: z.object({ /* … */ }),
  async handler(args, ctx) { /* … */ },
});
```

The trap: it's **per-tool**, so a family can drift — `search`/`remember` carried
it but `list`/`update`/`forget` silently didn't, so three of five memory tools
stayed broken for fleet sessions long after the first two were "fixed".

## Guard against re-opening it

When a tool family must all be cross-workspace, pin it with a one-line drift-guard
so a new tool (or a refactor) can't silently drop the flag — see
`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/memory/crossworkspace-invariant.test.ts`,
which imports every memory tool's real def and asserts `crossWorkspace === true`.

If you add a tool that reads a user/harness-scoped store (not `ctx.tx`) and want
it reachable from cups, set `crossWorkspace: true` and add it to that guard.
